details:
ASTRACARE – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring & Early Risk Detection System

ASTRACARE is a Python-based health monitoring prototype designed to support the physical and mental well-being of astronauts during space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard where mission teams can monitor important health indicators, identify unusual readings, and review changes in an astronaut's health over time.

How it works:
The application allows users to select crew profiles and enter or modify health readings such as heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO₂), sleep duration, physical activity, stress, and mood. It applies configurable, rule-based thresholds to identify readings that may require attention and generates alerts along with a demonstration health-risk score. Readings can be saved in a local SQLite database, allowing users to view historical trends, review mission timelines, and generate downloadable CSV and TXT health reports. It also supports importing external CSV data.

Benefits and intended impact:
Astronauts operate in challenging environments where physical and psychological health monitoring is essential. ASTRACARE brings multiple health indicators into one interface, making it easier for mission teams to review crew health information, notice potentially concerning changes, and maintain historical records. Its intended impact is to demonstrate how accessible software tools can support better health awareness and early attention to possible risks during long-duration space missions.

Technology used:
The project was developed using Python and Streamlit for the application and interactive dashboard, SQLite for local data storage, and data-processing and visualization libraries for health trends and reports. It is designed to run locally without requiring a continuous internet connection. No specialized hardware or live wearable integration is currently required.

Creativity and innovation:
ASTRACARE combines physical health monitoring, mental wellness indicators, configurable alerts, risk scoring, crew profiles, mission timelines, trend analytics, and downloadable reports in one astronaut-focused platform. Instead of displaying isolated readings, it provides a more organized view of crew health and changes across mission timelines.

Factors considered by the team:
Our team considered ease of use, clarity of health information, offline accessibility, data persistence, historical monitoring, and the importance of presenting alerts in an understandable way. We also considered the limitations of simulated data and the need for medically validated thresholds before real-world deployment.

ASTRACARE is currently a functional prototype using simulated or manually entered readings. Its future development could include real wearable-device integration, astronaut-specific health baselines, medically validated alert criteria, and stronger data security for operational use.
